record: Hong Kong Antiquities and Monuments Office register
facts: The documented hall was finished in 1750 and fully restored by 2011. The nearby guesthouse and school are distinct parts of the wider compound.

record: Hong Kong Antiquities and Monuments Office architectural and restoration notes
facts: The front has three bays and a raised drum platform on either side. Courts separate the three timber-roofed halls, with a side chamber on either side of the second court. The restoration removed modern paint from the brick wall and stone columns and restored traditional tile roofs and historic ornament.
The ancestral hall is recorded with a 5.1 metre HKPD base, 13.5 metre top and a measured building area of 389.18 square metres.
